docs.title: SmartTouch Cloud Platform
docs.text:
SmartTouch Cloud Platform helps teams build, connect, and deploy IoT-enabled digital experiences. It gives developers the tools to integrate devices, APIs, services, and secure application configuration.

Use this documentation to learn the platform, complete onboarding, build your first integration, and move confidently into production operations.

docs.title: What's SmartTouch?
docs.text:
SmartTouch is a cloud platform for connected device and IoT service development. It provides a common foundation for:

  • Device connectivity and onboarding
  • Secure API authentication
  • API exploration and testing
  • IoT service deployment
  • Local development setup
  • Secrets and configuration management

docs.title: For Developers
docs.text:
Start here if you are building applications, integrating devices, calling SmartTouch APIs, or deploying your first IoT service.

Follow this path:

  1. Review the Developer Journey
  2. Confirm the Prerequisites
  3. Learn the Platform Concepts
  4. Configure Authentication
  5. Make your First API Call
  6. Test the Device API
  7. Test the Deployment API

After onboarding, use the API Reference and API Playground to explore endpoints, validate requests, and test integrations.

docs.title: Build With Platform Features
docs.text:
Developers can use SmartTouch to:

  • Build secure API integrations
  • Connect and validate devices
  • Test API calls before writing production code
  • Run services locally during development
  • Configure secrets for applications and services
  • Resolve common onboarding and integration issues

If you are setting up your environment, begin with Set Up Local Development.

docs.title: SmartTouch RAG Answering
docs.text: This component parses MkDocs Markdown, preserves YAML front matter, splits content along heading and block boundaries, and emits deterministic JSONL records for a later embedding and vector-storage stage.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
From the ai-docs directory in the SmartTouch repository:

python -m ai_docs.ingest `
  --docs-root ../docs `
  --output build/chunks.jsonl `
  --exclude "test-*.md"

Each JSONL record includes:

  • a deterministic chunk ID and content hash;
  • source path, source URL, document title, heading, and heading hierarchy;
  • line locations, chunk index, and word count;
  • all source YAML front matter, including SmartTouch personas, tasks, tags, related documents, owners, review metadata, and retrieval questions.

docs.title: Test
docs.text: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

docs.title: SmartTouch AI docs
docs.text: Utilities for indexing, searching, and answering questions from SmartTouch documentation.

docs.title: Knowledge graph query expansion
docs.text: The AI docs service can build a lightweight knowledge graph from embedded documentation chunks and use it to expand retrieval queries.

docs.title: Build the knowledge graph
docs.text:
Run from the ai-docs directory:

python -m ai_docs.build_knowledge_graph `
  --input build/embedded-chunks.jsonl `
  --entities-output build/kg-entities.jsonl `
  --relationships-output build/kg-relationships.jsonl

This writes:

  • build/kg-entities.jsonl
  • build/kg-relationships.jsonl

These files are generated artifacts and should not be committed.

docs.title: Check knowledge graph availability
docs.text:
Start the API server, then call:

Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8000/diagnostics"

A healthy KG setup reports:

{
  "knowledge_graph_configured": true,
  "knowledge_graph_entities_path": "build\\kg-entities.jsonl",
  "knowledge_graph_relationships_path": "build\\kg-relationships.jsonl"
}

docs.title: Use KG expansion from the CLI
docs.text:
python -m ai_docs.retrieval_service_cli `
  --query "device cannot connect to broker" `
  --limit 3 `
  --format search `
  --use-knowledge-graph

For citation-ready context:

python -m ai_docs.retrieval_service_cli `
  --query "device cannot connect to broker" `
  --limit 3 `
  --format context `
  --use-knowledge-graph

For grounded answers:

python -m ai_docs.retrieval_service_cli `
  --query "device cannot connect to broker" `
  --limit 3 `
  --format answer `
  --use-knowledge-graph

docs.title: Use KG expansion from HTTP
docs.text:
Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8000/search" `
  -Method Post `
  -ContentType "application/json" `
  -Body '{"query":"device cannot connect to broker","limit":3,"use_knowledge_graph":true}'

The public response keeps the original user query. The expanded query is only used internally for retrieval.

docs.title: Test the Deployment API on Windows
docs.text: Use the local V2 sandbox to submit and inspect a deployment record. This workflow validates the REST contract; it does not build an image or deploy to a real Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Prepare a service request.
  2. Submit the deployment.
  3. Verify the deployment.

Use bearer token demo-token for every request.

docs.title: Prepare a service request
docs.text:
Create the request body in PowerShell:

$deployment = @{
  name = "temperature-service"
  environment = "dev"
  image = "ghcr.io/example/temperature-service:2.0.0"
  replicas = 2
  configuration = @{
    LOG_LEVEL = "info"
    DEVICE_FLEET = "factory-floor"
  }
  dry_run = $false
}

$body = $deployment | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4
$body

Valid environments are dev, staging, and prod. The local sandbox records the image name but does not pull or run the container.

Continue to Submit the deployment.

docs.title: Submit the deployment
docs.text:
Run this in the same PowerShell terminal where you created $body:

$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/services" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Post `
  -ContentType "application/json" `
  -Body $body

A successful request returns status 201 and a service whose status is healthy.

docs.title: API Playground
docs.text:
1. Open API Playground → Deployment API → V2.
  2. Authorize with demo-token.
  3. Open POST /v2/services.
  4. Paste the JSON request and send it.

Continue to Verify the deployment.

docs.title: Verify the deployment
docs.text:
Retrieve the deployment record:

$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/services/temperature-service?environment=dev" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

List every development service:

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/services?environment=dev&limit=20" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

To inspect the seeded example instead, request:

GET /v2/services/remote-access-service?environment=staging

The sandbox resets when the API process restarts. Use a database-backed implementation for persistent deployment state.

docs.title: Test the Device API on Windows
docs.text: Use PowerShell or the V2 API Playground to register and inspect devices in the local sandbox.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
• Start the V2 API on port 8090.
  • Start MkDocs on port 8001 if you want to use the Playground.
  • Use bearer token demo-token.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Register a test device.
  2. Inspect device details.
  3. Verify agent status.

The sandbox is in-memory. Restarting the API restores sensor-001 and sensor-002 and removes devices you registered.

docs.title: PowerShell
docs.text:
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }
$body = @{
  id = "sensor-003"
  display_name = "Pressure Sensor 003"
  fleet = "factory-floor"
  agent_version = "2.0.0"
  labels = @{
    site = "pune"
    criticality = "medium"
  }
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Post `
  -ContentType "application/json" `
  -Body $body

The new device starts with agent_status set to unknown because the sandbox does not run a physical device agent.

docs.title: API Playground
docs.text:
1. Open API Playground → Device API → V2.
  2. Authorize with demo-token.
  3. Open POST /v2/devices.
  4. Paste the JSON equivalent of the PowerShell body.
  5. Send the request and confirm status 201.

Continue to Inspect device details.

docs.title: Inspect device details
docs.text:
List the available devices:

$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }

$response = Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices?fleet=factory-floor&limit=10" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

$response.data | Format-Table id, display_name, agent_status, agent_version

Retrieve the device registered in the previous step:

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices/sensor-003" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

Use sensor-001 if you restarted the API and the custom device is no longer present.

docs.title: Physical device boundary
docs.text:
The local service simulates registry data only. Installing a real remote-access agent, provisioning certificates, and managing a Linux device service are outside the local Windows sandbox.

Continue to Verify agent status.

docs.title: Verify device agent status
docs.text:
Use the seeded online device for a positive test:

$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices/sensor-001/agent-status" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

Expected values include:

device_id    : sensor-001
agent_status : online
latency_ms   : 12

Other useful tests:

  • sensor-002 returns offline.
  • A newly registered sensor-003 returns unknown.
  • sensor-999 returns 404 Not Found.

You can send the same requests from API Playground → Device API → V2.

docs.title: Set up local development on Windows
docs.text:
This journey uses native Windows PowerShell. It runs the MkDocs portal on port 8001 and the FastAPI V2 sandbox on port 8090.

You do not need WSL2, Linux, Kubernetes, or stctl for the local documentation and API workflows.

docs.title: Journey
docs.text: Step Topic Outcome 1 Set up Windows API tools Python, MkDocs, and API dependencies are ready 2 Optional Kubernetes access kubectl is ready when a real cluster is available 3 Run the portal and API locally MkDocs and the V2 sandbox run together

docs.title: Local addresses
docs.text:
Component Address MkDocs portal http://127.0.0.1:8001/SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform/ API health http://127.0.0.1:8090/health FastAPI documentation http://127.0.0.1:8090/docs OpenAPI document http://127.0.0.1:8090/openapi.json

Use bearer token demo-token when testing the local V2 APIs.

docs.title: Set up Windows API tools
docs.text: Prepare a native Windows PowerShell environment for the SmartTouch documentation portal and runnable V2 API sandbox. WSL2 and the unavailable stctl CLI are not required.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Windows 10 or Windows 11
  • PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell 5.1
  • Python 3.12
  • Git
  • Visual Studio Code

docs.title: 1. Open the repository
docs.text: Set-Location "C:\Users\chris\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform\GitHub\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform"

docs.title: 2. Create and activate the virtual environment
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

If the prompt already begins with (.venv), the environment is active and you can skip this step.

docs.title: 3. Install the API and documentation tools
docs.text:
python -m pip install -r .\services\platform-api-v2\requirements.txt
python -m pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material pymdown-extensions

docs.title: 4. Verify the tools
docs.text:
python --version
mkdocs --version

docs.title: 5. Configure the local API token
docs.text:
The reference service accepts this development-only bearer token:

$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_V2_TOKEN = "demo-token"

The value applies only to the current PowerShell session. Do not use this token for a production service.

Continue to Run the portal and API locally.

docs.title: Optional: configure Kubernetes on Windows
docs.text: Kubernetes is not required for the local V2 API sandbox. Complete this page only when an administrator has given you access to a real Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: 1. Install kubectl
docs.text:
winget install --exact --id Kubernetes.kubectl

Open a new terminal and verify the installation:

kubectl version --client

docs.title: 2. Install the supplied kubeconfig
docs.text:
Obtain a kubeconfig from your SmartTouch administrator and save it to:

C:\Users\<your-user>\.kube\config

List the available contexts and select the assigned context:

kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl config use-context <context-name>

docs.title: 3. Verify access
docs.text:
kubectl get namespaces
kubectl get pods --namespace smarttouch-remote-access

If you receive an authentication or authorization error, contact the cluster administrator. The local repository cannot create production cluster credentials.

Continue to Run the portal and API locally.

docs.title: Run the portal and API locally
docs.text: Run the API and MkDocs in two PowerShell terminals.

docs.title: Terminal 1: start the V2 API
docs.text:
Set-Location "C:\Users\chris\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform\GitHub\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform"
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_V2_TOKEN = "demo-token"
Set-Location .\services\platform-api-v2
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8090

Keep this terminal running. Verify the service from another terminal:

Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/health"

docs.title: Terminal 2: start MkDocs
docs.text:
Set-Location "C:\Users\chris\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform\GitHub\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform"
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
mkdocs serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8001

Open http://127.0.0.1:8001/SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform/.

docs.title: Test the Device API from PowerShell
docs.text:
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices?limit=10" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

docs.title: Test from the portal
docs.text:
1. Open API Playground → Device API → V2.
  2. Select Authorize and enter demo-token.
  3. Open GET /v2/devices.
  4. Set limit to 10 and send the request.

The response contains the seeded devices sensor-001 and sensor-002.

docs.title: Stop the services
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+C in each server terminal. Then deactivate the Python environment:

deactivate

docs.title: Developer journey on Windows
docs.text: Use native PowerShell and the runnable REST API sandbox to learn SmartTouch. The journey does not require WSL2 or stctl.

docs.title: Journey
docs.text:
1. Confirm the prerequisites.
  2. Review the platform concepts.
  3. Configure local authentication.
  4. Make your first API call.
  5. Use common errors when a request fails.

docs.title: What you will use
docs.text:
• PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod for command-line API calls
  • The V2 API sandbox at http://127.0.0.1:8090
  • The MkDocs API Playground at http://127.0.0.1:8001/SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform/
  • Development bearer token demo-token

The local service contains seeded Device, Deployment, and Audit Log data. Changes are stored in memory and reset when the API restarts.

docs.title: Authenticate to the local API
docs.text: The V2 reference service uses a development-only bearer token.

docs.title: PowerShell
docs.text:
Set the token for the current terminal and create a reusable header:

$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_TOKEN = "demo-token"
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:SMARTTOUCH_API_TOKEN" }

Verify the token against the Device API:

Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices?limit=1" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

docs.title: API Playground
docs.text:
1. Open a V2 Playground page.
  2. Select Authorize.
  3. Enter demo-token without the Bearer prefix.
  4. Apply the credentials and send the request.

docs.title: Security boundary
docs.text: demo-token is only for the local sandbox. A deployed environment must use an identity provider or another production authentication mechanism. Never commit real tokens to Git.

docs.title: Connection refused on port 8090
docs.text:
The API is not running. Start it from services\platform-api-v2:

$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_V2_TOKEN = "demo-token"
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8090

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
The bearer token is missing or incorrect. Use:

$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }

In the Playground, enter only demo-token in the authorization dialog.

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
Check both the API version and resource identifier. Valid local examples include:

GET /v2/devices/sensor-001
GET /v2/devices/sensor-002

The service root is http://127.0.0.1:8090/; V2 endpoints begin with /v2.

docs.title: Browser CORS error
docs.text: Open the portal from http://127.0.0.1:8001, not from a generated HTML file on disk. The API allows the documented local portal origins.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
Identify the process using the port:

Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8001,8090 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Select-Object LocalPort, State, OwningProcess

Stop the previous MkDocs or Uvicorn terminal with Ctrl+C, then restart it.

docs.title: Activation script is blocked
docs.text:
Allow locally created scripts for your user account:

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned

Run the command only if your organization permits this policy change.

docs.title: Make your first API call
docs.text: List the devices seeded in the local V2 service.

docs.title: PowerShell
docs.text:
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer demo-token" }

$response = Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices?limit=10" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

$response.data | Format-Table id, display_name, fleet, agent_status

Expected devices:

ID Fleet Status sensor-001 factory-floor online sensor-002 factory-floor offline

docs.title: Filter the list
docs.text:
Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices?status=online&fleet=factory-floor&limit=10" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

docs.title: Get one device
docs.text:
Invoke-RestMethod `
  -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/devices/sensor-001" `
  -Headers $headers `
  -Method Get

docs.title: Repeat the request in the Playground
docs.text:
1. Open API Playground → Device API → V2.
  2. Authorize with demo-token.
  3. Open GET /v2/devices/{device_id}.
  4. Enter sensor-001 for device_id.
  5. Send the request.

Continue to the Device API V2 Reference for the complete contract.

docs.title: API Reference and API Playground
docs.text:
The API Reference is read-only documentation. Use it to inspect endpoints, parameters, schemas, and responses.

The API Playground is interactive. Use it to authorize and send requests to a configured server.

docs.title: V1 and V2
docs.text:
• V1 documents the original contracts and uses placeholder platform addresses.
  • V2 provides runnable Device, Deployment, and Audit Log endpoints through the local FastAPI service.

Choose V2 when you want to test requests locally.

Browser

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All V2 business endpoints require an HTTP bearer token. The local sandbox accepts demo-token. The Playground adds the Bearer prefix after you authorize.

docs.title: Data lifecycle
docs.text: The local V2 service uses an in-memory store with seeded examples. Restarting the API restores the original devices, deployment, and audit events.

docs.title: Workstation
docs.text:
• Windows 10 or Windows 11
  • PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell 5.1
  • Python 3.12
  • Git
  • Visual Studio Code

docs.title: Repository
docs.text:
Open PowerShell in the repository root:

Set-Location "C:\Users\chris\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform\GitHub\SmartTouch-Cloud-Platform"

Confirm the expected branch and Python version:

git branch --show-current
python --version

docs.title: Running services
docs.text:
Complete Set up local development on Windows. Then verify:

Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8090/health"

The result must show status as UP before you use the API Playground.

docs.title: Browser
docs.text: Use a current version of Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, or Firefox. The portal and API must both be running because the Playground sends requests from port 8001 to port 8090.

docs.title: Configuration and secrets on Windows
docs.text:
The local V2 sandbox supports non-sensitive service configuration in Deployment API requests. It does not include Vault or another production secret manager.

Use this section to:

  • set local values with PowerShell environment variables;
  • send non-sensitive configuration through the Deployment API;
  • keep credentials out of source control and API payloads; and
  • understand the V2 deployment request fields.

For local API calls, use the development bearer token demo-token. Replace it with an approved identity and secret-management solution before production deployment.

docs.title: V2 deployment request schema
docs.text:
POST /v2/services accepts the following JSON object:

Field Type Required Notes name string Yes Lowercase service name, 3–63 characters environment string Yes dev, staging, or prod image string Yes Container image reference recorded by the sandbox replicas integer No From 1 to 100; defaults to 1 configuration object No Non-sensitive string key/value pairs dry_run boolean No Validates without saving when true

Example:

{
  "name": "temperature-service",
  "environment": "dev",
  "image": "ghcr.io/example/temperature-service:2.0.0",
  "replicas": 2,
  "configuration": {
    "LOG_LEVEL": "info",
    "DEVICE_FLEET": "factory-floor"
  },
  "dry_run": false
}

Use API Playground → Deployment API → V2 to validate and send the request.

docs.title: PowerShell environment variables
docs.text:
Set values for the current terminal session:

$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_V2_TOKEN = "demo-token"
$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8090"

Read them without printing the token:

$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_BASE_URL
if ($env:SMARTTOUCH_API_V2_TOKEN) { "Token is configured" }

Close the terminal to discard session-scoped variables.

docs.title: Service configuration
docs.text:
The Deployment API accepts non-sensitive configuration:

$deployment = @{
  name = "temperature-service"
  environment = "dev"
  image = "ghcr.io/example/temperature-service:2.0.0"
  replicas = 2
  configuration = @{
    LOG_LEVEL = "info"
    DEVICE_FLEET = "factory-floor"
  }
  dry_run = $false
}

Do not place passwords, tokens, private keys, or connection strings in the configuration object.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Use PowerShell environment variables for temporary local values:

$env:SMARTTOUCH_API_V2_TOKEN = "demo-token"
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:SMARTTOUCH_API_V2_TOKEN" }

Do not save real credentials in Markdown, source code, .env files committed to Git, OpenAPI examples, or Deployment API payloads.

docs.title: Repository protection
docs.text:
Before committing, inspect staged changes:

git diff --cached

If a real secret is committed, rotate it immediately and remove it using your organization's incident procedure. Deleting the line in a later commit does not remove the value from Git history.

docs.title: Production environments
docs.text:
The reference repository does not implement production secret storage. A production deployment should inject secrets from an approved service such as a cloud secret manager, Kubernetes Secrets with encryption controls, or Vault.

Keep secret values separate from the V2 configuration object. Applications should receive them at runtime through the selected secret provider.

docs.title: Audit Log API v2 Playground
docs.text:
